transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25 16:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Liu (Redwood SE), Ben Ortiz (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Silverpine - Security Lead), Elena Gomez (Platform Eng), Tomas Berg (DevOps), Naomi Choi (Compliance)

[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining really appreciate you making time, quick agenda—cover SAML attributes, SCIM provisioning options, then role slicing and audit requirements, and action items. ok?
[00:18] Ravi Menon: yep that's perfect, we mostly want to validate this fits with our SOC 2 plan and the EU data residency constraints we have for some funds.
[00:30] Maya Liu: cool, I'll go slow on the SAML bits i know those can be hairy, and Ben will jump in on KMS/audit log pieces.
[00:42] Elena Gomez: just to flag we already have Okta as the IdP and a separate Azure AD for some contractors, and staging/prod are in different cloud accounts.
[00:55] Tomas Berg: also we rotate service-account keys every 30 days and want to avoid long-lived tokens on the platform side.
[01:07] Jordan Park: noted. quick question — are you planning SCIM push from Okta for groups or just SAML group assertions?
[01:18] Ravi Menon: prefer SCIM push for automated provisioning, but for some legacy apps we'll need assertion-based roles; we want group membership to drive RBAC.
[01:31] Maya Liu: makes sense. for SCIM we typically recommend group-based provisioning with an externalId to map to role IDs, and then we do a light reconciliation check during login in case of drift.
[01:44] Ben Ortiz: one thing to watch: SCIM filtering capabilities vary by IdP and can cause over-provisioning if not scoped properly — Okta supports group filters but you'll want to avoid syncing the entire org.
[01:58] Elena Gomez: yep that's our worry, we have hundreds of groups. we want a handful that map to least-privilege role slices.
[02:10] Jordan Park: let's talk role slices — what does Silverpine consider a minimal role set?
[02:19] Ravi Menon: at high level: org-admin (very restricted), infra-admin (deploy and infra config), model-ops (manage model versions and deployments), app-ops (service owners), billing/view-only. plus a service-account role for CI.
[02:34] Maya Liu: that's a good starting point. recommended pattern: prefer breadth over depth — create narrow roles (e.g., model-deploy-only) and compose for power users via role assignment rather than large monolithic admin roles.
[02:48] Tomas Berg: how do we handle cross-account resources? e.g., staging has different resource tags.
[02:55] Ben Ortiz: we use resource scoping in RBAC rules, so roles include allowed namespaces/env tags. that way infra-admin in staging doesn't automatically get prod access.
[03:11] Jordan Park: on SAML attributes — the important ones for Redwood are: nameid/email, groups, and we support a roles claim if you want to push role IDs directly. the assertion can include a roles claim or just groups and we map groups to role IDs on our side.
[03:29] Ravi Menon: our IdP currently sends groups as a long string and sometimes truncates in SAML. that has bitten us before.
[03:39] Maya Liu: yeah that happens. recommended: use SCIM for provisioning group membership when possible, and SAML groups for session-level checks only. also we can accept a custom SAML attribute (roles) which is just role IDs — reduces parsing problems.
[03:56] Elena Gomez: if we send role IDs directly we can avoid extra mapping logic, but it means more coordination on naming.
[04:06] Ben Ortiz: tradeoff: direct role IDs are simpler but less flexible; group-to-role mapping lets you change mappings without IdP changes.
[04:18] Tomas Berg: about deprovisioning — we need guaranteed immediate removal for terminated employees. how fast does SCIM deprovision?
[04:26] Maya Liu: SCIM push is near-real time from Okta (usually under a minute for single change), but recon jobs run at intervals. for safety we also block tokens on deprovision events and support immediate revocation via API.
[04:40] Naomi Choi: audit logs are critical for SOC 2 — retention, integrity, and encryption. what format and retention do you support?
[04:50] Ben Ortiz: Redwood provides JSON-formatted audit logs with event types, actor, resource, and token-id. default retention for hosted is 90 days but for enterprise/private we can extend to 12+ months to meet SOC 2. logs are tamper-evident and signed; you can export to your SIEM via S3 or syslog.
[05:09] Ravi Menon: we need 12 months immutable retention and monthly export to our S3 bucket in eu-central region.
[05:17] Ben Ortiz: fine — we can set up a cross-account S3 export with server-side encryption using your KMS key. that keeps keys in your control.
[05:27] Elena Gomez: how does KMS integration work? do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:33] Maya Liu: yes, for Private deployments we support HSM-backed CMKs via KMS and we can also integrate with cloud KMS for Dedicated with key access controls. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and support rotating the envelope keys on a schedule.
[05:48] Ravi Menon: any impacts to latency when using customer-managed keys?
[05:53] Ben Ortiz: minimal — KMS ops are at provisioning time for tokens and secrets; runtime token validation uses cached materials. we measure <5ms added on average.
[06:03] Jordan Park: circling back to least-privilege — we'd recommend implementing permission boundaries and ephemeral role grants for on-call or emergency operations.
[06:14] Elena Gomez: can you give an example?
[06:17] Maya Liu: sure. say infra-admin normally can't modify production model configs; create an "elevated-session" flow that issues a short-lived privilege token for max 30 minutes requiring MFA and an approval workflow.
[06:31] Tomas Berg: that would help with our compliance reviewers.
[06:34] Naomi Choi: about data residency — we have funds that require EU data never leave eu-central. how do you ensure telemetry and logs stay in-region?
[06:44] Ben Ortiz: we have region-aware routing; for Private customers you can run the control plane in your VPC and configure all logs/metrics to stream to your region. for hosted we can pin storage and logs to eu-central and route inference to regional infra.
[06:58] Ravi Menon: any caveats on backups or analytics?
[07:02] Maya Liu: analytics pipelines sometimes aggregate across regions unless you opt out — we can provide an isolated analytics path for EU-resident workloads. we'll include notes in the SSO playbook.
[07:14] Jordan Park: let's cover a rough rollout plan: phase 1 — staging SCIM with 5 pilot groups; phase 2 — prod SCIM cutover for non-critical teams; phase 3 — roles audit and remediation, and SOC2 artifacts collection. thoughts?
[07:29] Elena Gomez: sounds good. pilot groups: infra, model-ops, app-ops, billing, svc-accounts.
[07:36] Tomas Berg: svc-accounts are tricky — we want long-term certs managed via KMS and short-lived creds for pipelines.
[07:44] Ben Ortiz: recommended: use service-account role with client-certificate rotation and KMS-protected private keys; SCIM can still own the account object but the secrets live in your secret store.
[07:57] Ravi Menon: on the audit side, will you include token IDs and request traces so we can correlate with our SIEM?
[08:05] Ben Ortiz: yes, token-id and trace-id are included and we can tag events with tenant and org IDs. we also provide a trace export for a specific timeframe for audits.
[08:19] Maya Liu: i'll share a sample SCIM mapping sheet — include columns: IdP group id, IdP group name, Redwood role id, externalId, filter expression, target envs.
[08:30] Jordan Park: one more gotcha — SCIM group sync sometimes creates duplicate groups if displayName changes; best to use externalId on group objects for stable mapping.
[08:41] Elena Gomez: ok we'll plan to add externalId to our Okta provisioning rules.
[08:47] Tomas Berg: testing plan — create three test users (one EU-resident), ensure SCIM creates group membership, then run login flow and confirm assertion claims; collect audit logs for 48 hours.
[09:00] Naomi Choi: we'll also want a runbook for incident response that includes steps to revoke session tokens and rotate keys.
[09:08] Ben Ortiz: we can provide a runbook template and an API call list for emergency revocation.
[09:15] Jordan Park: ok let's summarize action items — Maya will send mapping and SAML samples; Ben will send KMS/audit notes; Ravi provides Okta admin and staging tenant; schedule hands-on SCIM session next week.
[09:30] Ravi Menon: good, thanks everyone.
[09:34] Jordan Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlaps and mis-heard acronyms (eg: "K-V cache" for KV cache) — cleaned slightly but left pauses and repeats to preserve speech patterns.
